messages:
alex (support): FYI customer ACME (acct acme-prod) opened an escalation — they received sustained 429s from 11:12–11:45 UTC yesterday, but Console shows ~120M tokens remaining for their org. They're escalating to us. attaching customer sample request IDs and error screenshots. https://redwood.app/attachments/acc-123/429s.png

maria (sre): can you drop 2-3 request ids and the X-Request-ID from the failed responses? also what plan/org-id did they query?

alex (support): sent two sample headers + body:
```
X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d
Response: {"error":"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED","code":429}
Response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 100000000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1720000000
Org: org-acme-prod
```
Customer screenshot shows Console -> Quota page at 11:30 UTC: Available tokens 120,334,210.

kevin (telemetry): ingestion latency was normal (~10–30s) at that window from metrics pipeline. But metrics and enforcement read from different stores: console uses quota-summary table (periodic aggregate), enforcement service talks to quota-reservoir (redis). We should check both.

sophia (eng-infra): copying the enforcement team. quick checks: quota-summary-writer had a consumer lag spike around 11:08–11:20 UTC on cluster kafka-2. Not huge but a partition reassignment happened. I'll paste consumer-group output:
```
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-2:9092 --describe --group quota-summary-writer
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
quota-events    3          742091          742991          900
```

maria (sre): 900 lag ~ a few minutes worth. not enough to explain 30+ minute discrepancy. any infra events?

sophia (eng-infra): there was a rolling restart of redis-cluster-primary at 11:05 UTC due to maintenance. It failed over and one shard came up in read-only mode for ~18 minutes before auto-recovery. enforcement reads were hitting the failing shard, which returned stale counters (could return 0 remaining) while the aggregator (which writes to the summary table) was still processing events. so console saw aggregated view later.

kevin (telemetry): that matches: enforcement logs show repeated Redis NIL or ERR READONLY during the window: snippet: `ERR READONLY You can't write against a read only replica.` enforcement then fell back to local in-memory leaky-bucket with conservative defaults and started returning 429s.

alex (support): so high-level: enforcement service saw redis failover, rewrote to local fallback (much lower limits) -> customers saw 429s. Console reads summary table which still showed tokens until aggregator caught up. that explains discrepancy.

maria (sre): immediate customer remediation done?

alex (support): we issued temporary credit refund for the 33 minutes, notified customer about root cause and that we would reconcile backfill. customer accepted and asked for postmortem.

sophia (eng-infra): mitigation steps taken: 1) restarted quota-enforcement pods to clear fallback state 2) forced redis failover fix and scaled replicas 3) kicked quota-aggregator backfill for the window. commands used: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/quota-enforcement` and `quota-aggregator backfill --org org-acme-prod --start 2026-06-20T11:00:00Z --end 2026-06-20T12:00:00Z`

kevin (telemetry): backfill completed and summary table updated at 11:58 UTC. enforcement no longer returned 429s after restart.

tim (product): action items we should track for next week: - add monitor for Redis READONLY errors on primary - alert if quota-enforcement falls into fallback mode - audit runbook for maintenance windows so we don't trigger forced read-only shards without coordinated throttle changes.

maria (sre): also adding consumer-lag alert threshold: if lag > 5m then page and if aggregate lag causes mismatch between enforcement and console for >10m, escalate.

alex (support): customer follow-up: sent them timeline + credits + ETA for postmortem. they replied :thumbsup: and said 'appreciate the quick fix, plz keep us posted on postmortem.'

sophia (eng-infra): long-term fix proposals (will put in a ticket): - make enforcement resilient to READONLY by reading fallback counters from a replicated snapshot rather than entering tiny local buckets - add a reconciliation handshake where enforcement checks summary-table delta before switching to fallback for large orgs - add tests simulating redis failover during writes.

kevin (telemetry): I'll add dashboard panels to show enforcement fallback state and redis replica health side-by-side for the top 50 orgs.

alex (support): great. closing thread when postmortem ticket is created. thanks team :raised_hands:

acme-customer-bot: Support case #INC-2026-1789 was resolved by credits and root-cause identified.

maria (sre): ticket created: INFRA-4821 "Quota enforcement fallback on redis read-only during maintenance -> customer 429s" assigned to eng-infra. planning weekly follow-up.
